It’s disheartening to write a negative review about Idli Dosa Fusion, Malad East, especially since I’ve always appreciated their food quality. However, my recent experience was far from satisfactory.

Service and Hygiene Concerns:

Upon ordering a Masala Dosa, Thate Idli, and Filter Coffee, I was surprised to see the Dosa served on a small paper plate, with the masala in a paper cup typically used for tea. Chutney and Sambar were also served in similar paper cups. The staff mentioned that the cutlery washer was unavailable, but this setup was both unexpected and uncomfortable.

The Thate Masala Idli was presented in the same manner. Additionally, I had to request the staff three times to clean the table, and it was only addressed when I insisted that they take the food back if the table wasn’t cleaned.

Filter Coffee Issue:

The Filter Coffee was initially served in an unclean cup with dried coffee stains. When I pointed this out, the staff claimed it was clean until I showed them the stains, after which they provided a paper cup. I had asked to cancel the coffee order, but they refused, stating it couldn’t be returned.

Lack of Management Communication:

When I expressed my desire to share this feedback with the owner, the staff informed me they didn’t have his contact number.

Suggestions for Improvement:

While I value the taste of the food at IDF, such lapses in service and hygiene are unacceptable. I urge the management to:
•	Ensure proper cutlery and serving dishes are available at all times.
•	Maintain cleanliness, especially given the outlet’s proximity to the road, which can lead to dust accumulation on tables.
•	Provide facilities for customers to wash their hands.
•	Train staff to handle customer concerns with honesty and promptness.

Given the presence of competitors nearby, it’s crucial not to lose loyal customers due to avoidable issues. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and implements necessary changes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited the newly renovated Shree Laxmi Vilas Bar in Malad East, and while there are a few things to appreciate, the overall experience ended up being a mixed bag — definitely not beyond 3 stars.

To begin with the positives, the renovation is genuinely impressive. The place looks fresh, modern, and much more inviting compared to most local bars in the area. The interior design is clean, well-lit, and thoughtfully done. The seating layout is comfortable and the ambience gives the feeling of a higher-end local bar. Even the crowd seemed more decent and composed than what you would typically expect in similar neighbourhood bars. This immediately makes the place feel safer and more comfortable, especially if you’re coming with friends.

However, the experience fell apart when it came to service and food, which are two of the most important aspects of any bar or restaurant. The waiter was completely inattentive — barely making eye contact, not checking on the table, and showing no interest in assisting with the order. When we pointed out issues, there was hardly any response.

The worst part was the Chicken Lollipop we ordered. The outer coating was extremely hard — so hard that it was difficult to bite into — but the waiter didn’t seem bothered at all. There was no attempt to replace it, apologise, or even acknowledge the complaint. It felt like the staff was simply not trained or not interested in customer satisfaction. The rest of the food was mediocre at best, definitely not worth the price they charge. For the kind of rates we paid, the quality should have been far better. It felt more like regular bar food but priced as premium.

They do have a smoking room, which is appreciated, but it clearly doesn’t match the new interiors. It looks old, under-maintained, and completely out of sync with the renovated main area. If they’ve taken the effort to upgrade the interior, the smoking room should be improved to the same standard.

Overall, Shree Laxmi Vilas Bar has potential — good ambience, good crowd, and a newly upgraded environment — but the poor service and disappointing food really pull the entire experience down. A place with such nice interiors should ideally offer much better hospitality. For now, it remains an average experience at best.

featured_reviews.name: Manpreet Bhamra
featured_reviews.review_text:
For anyone who enjoys authentic south indian food, this is an okay place. Fair warning: food is strictly vegetarian.

Special thanks to our hosts for the evening Ms. Shivani and Mr. Raj for their hospitality. They helped us understand and pick dishes from the menu.

Kamat's Legacy serves unlimited Thali for lunch/dinner/breakfast. I tried the unlimited Thali for dinner but sadly it's not at par with other unlimited thali options that I have tried. The food is served hot and fresh but the amount and variety of dishes in are severely limited. Just about 4-5 dishes which includes the curries, no sambar or rasam are included which is really odd and the cost of this thali is ₹550 which is not justified.

Then comes the service: usually places offering unlimited thali (such as Maharaja Bhog or Jain Sabkuch) have an entire entourage of multiple servers constantly refilling your food without having to ask. There is no such system here. You have to request for refill every time and each time it takes them up to 5-10 minutes to get your dishes which breaks the tempo of eating.

I would rather prefer Jain Sabkuch or Maharajag Bhog if I really want to try the unlimited veg thali experience. Their service is top notch and the variety/amount of dishes offered is also better and at the same price as the unlimited thali served here.

We also ordered Bisi Bheli Bhaat and Podi Idli apart from the thali which were also disappointing. The quantity of food being served for the a la carte dishes doesn't justify the price of those items. For Podi Idli, we only got 3 medium sized idlis.

The quantity and quality of the food versus the price was a letdown which is why I don't really recommend this place that much. I also don't understand why there is an additional "service charge" included in our bill which is additional to the GST and CGST which we are already paying.

The only redeeming quality of our experience was the assortment of chutneys and pickles which is why I give it at least 2 stars.
